mutant.description: NOT a planted byte mutation, and the reason is recorded rather than glossed: every limb of this act's claim lives on the live S3/host plane or in an append-only shared file, so planting would have meant mutating served state or creating a transient false OPEN that a peer's deploy_ledger.py check --red sweep could escalate on. The DEPLOY genre exists for this case but is NOT claimed: the governing order carries <risk>WORLD</risk> and no <proof_genre>DEPLOY</proof_genre> line at HEAD, and DEPLOY is never self-declared. The controls used instead are STATE-BASED and arose naturally from an order that applied twice. (1) THE AC1 THREE-STATE CONTROL. (2) THE BASE/CUT DISCRIMINATION PAIR, run on both applies and in both directions. (3) THE AC2 NEGATIVE ARM at the pre-round base. (4) A NAME-DROP CONTROL on the tool census. (5) THE BUN PRE-CHECK's two arms. (6) THE HALT GATE's refusal/admission pair -- see the honest note on two VOID attempts below. (7) THE V2 CUT-METHOD CONTROL against the trunk.

The v1 branch read 'Any other read-back fails, including r11.AC2 or r11.AC3 -> redeploy the versioned base artifact; the ledger closes ROLLED-BACK, plus a BLOCKING row.' It is written for a read-back that MEASURES THE ACT GOING WRONG, and every read of the v1 act was clean: 107 of 107 byte-identical to the build input with a discriminating negative control, /health 200, tools 67 = 67 by name, .env 54 = 54, ids 7 = 7, AC3 PASS. DIRECT PRECEDENT, same project, one release back: MX-r-10's instance declares the identical exclusion when r10.AC2 first read FAIL, and that issuer amended rather than rolled back. The fix-forward then proved the reasoning: the same criterion PASSES on v2 with definitions 67 of 67, and the pre-round artifact was never disturbed.
